full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that opposite party No. 2 Md. Asgar Ali as plaintiff instituted a suit in, the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Thakurgaon being Title Suit No. 20 of 1986, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in `ka' schedule land after demolishing the structures standing thereon and for permanent injunction in respect of the remaining portion of the suit land restraining the defendants from interfering with his possession in the suit property in any way interfering with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs, therein. The plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land measuring 1.59 acres belonged to Syed Mesbahuddoza, Syed Anwaruddoza and Chowdhury Md. Ilyas. Chowdhury Md. Ilyas died leaving son Chowdhury Matiar Rahman. Subsequently, Syed Mesbahuddoza and Syed Anwaruddoza appointed Anwar Ahmed as their constituted attorney while Chowdhury Matiar. Rahman appointed Pyar Ali as his constituted attorney. In course of time, the landlords settled 15 decimals of the land of Plot No. 34 with Abdul Gafur, who owned and possessed the same and his name has been duly recorded in the S. A. Khatian. Defendant's father Abdus Salam Sarker purchased the same land from Abdul Gafur by a registered kabala dated 30.1.86 and since then he has been living there with the members of his family by constructing a house therein. Thereafter Abdus Salam Sarker again purchased 5 decimals of land by a kabala dated 5.4.75 from Baharuddin, who had earlier purchased the same. Abdus Salam Sarker against purchased 22 decimals of land from the recorded tenants by a kabala dated 31.7.75 and in this way he became the owner to the extent of 42i decimals of land and in due course of time he got the said land mutated in his name by opening a knew khatian, following which he paid rent to the appropriate authority. Thereafter Abdus Salam Sarker transferred 12 decimals of land to Rekha Rani and 5 decimal of land to the plaintiff on 16.6.80. The plaintiff thereafter purchased 3 decimal of land from Rekha Rani by a kabala dated 8.3.82. In this way, the plaintiff claims 16i decimals of land from the suit land. It has been alleged that the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff from 141 decimal of land described in schedule 'ka' to the plaint by constructing a house thereon on 1.4.96. When the defendants further threatened to dispossess him from .the remaining portion of the suit land described in schedule 'kha' to the plaint, the plaintiff has been constrained to filing the suit.
